_comment: The exceptions to arthome-check-enums, EACH WITH ITS REASON.
This file stays short or the rule is a bad one. Past twenty lines, that is
the sign that a value is missing from @arthome/core — not that the gate is
A legitimate exception has a recognisable shape: the value belongs to a
SPACE SHARED by two distinct vocabularies, and importing the constant would
be SEMANTICALLY WRONG. Any other justification is suspect.

allow.reason: TRUSTED_PROXIES' explicit word for 'no proxy fronts this BFF', a deployment setting. REPLAY_POLICIES, LANGUAGE_DEPENDENCIES, WATCH_SCOPES, WATCH_FALLBACK_ACTIONS and AUDIENCE_SANCTIONS each have a `none` member about a show, a viewer or a sanction; importing any of them to read an environment variable would name the wrong concept.

NODE_ENV's deployment mode, not a role on a show. MEMBER_ROLES has a `production` member because somebody works IN production — the crew sense — and the two share the English word without sharing anything else. Importing MEMBER_ROLES.PRODUCTION to describe how a process was started would carve the confusion in rather than correct it. This is the exact shape the gate has produced a bad fix for before: an agent once reached for NavigationEntry.JOURNAL to name an accounting export format, the same string and the wrong concept.

A tab of `/v1/search`, which storefront.yaml declares `x-arthome-vocabulary-source: none`: a property of that endpoint's list, not of the domain. PLAN_OPENINGS' `replays` is what a plan opens and NAVIGATION_ENTRIES' is a menu entry; importing either to name a search tab would be the NavigationEntry.JOURNAL mistake again.

A kind of page `resolvePublicLink` names, which storefront.yaml declares `x-arthome-vocabulary-source: none`. MEMBER_ROLES' `artist` is a role a person holds in a channel; a link to an artist's page is not a role.

The table of the Artist aggregate, named for the aggregate as `show`, `date` and `venue` are. MEMBER_ROLES' `artist` is a role a person holds in a channel, not the channel's public face this table stores.

A message's disposition: this message-id was already applied. REFUND_REASONS' `duplicate` is why money went back to a viewer charged twice. The two share the English word and nothing else; every consumer returns `Outcome.DUPLICATE`, so this definition is the only place the literal stands.

The table of the Seat entity (data-model.md §3.3), named for it as `seat_hold` and `seat_order` are. ORDER_KINDS' `seat` is a kind of order, not a table: importing OrderKind.SEAT to name one would be the NavigationEntry.JOURNAL mistake again.

OpenSearch's normalizer type: a `custom` normalizer is one this index assembles from its own filters, a word of the OpenSearch settings API. SCHEMA_ISSUE_RULES' `custom` is the rule of a failed refinement in `api.schema_invalid`; importing it to configure an index would name the wrong concept.

BullMQ's worker event for a failed job, the name `@OnWorkerEvent` listens under (`WorkerListener`). ORDER_STATES' `failed` is an order that took no payment; importing OrderState.FAILED to name a queue event would be the NavigationEntry.JOURNAL mistake again.

ioredis's connection status, the word its client reports once it answers commands. REPLAY_ASSET_STATES' `ready` is a replay that can be watched; importing ReplayAssetState.READY to read a Redis connection would be the NavigationEntry.JOURNAL mistake again.
